aAbout: God's Eye View is an open-source 3D world globe simulator — 'a spy-satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real.' It renders Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles through Cesium and layers live aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, traffic and public cameras from open sources, all processed locally in your browser. It went viral in 2026 for its voice-controlled AI agent, cockpit view and sensor-style visual modes. It is software you run yourself — via Pinokio one-click, a terminal install, or Docker — not a website you open.

aLink.label: WorldEye: the God's Eye View alternative

aStrengths: God's Eye View is the more spectacular and the more ownable tool: a photorealistic 3D globe with cockpit view, 3D aircraft models, sensor looks (FLIR, night vision) and a scene director for cinematic tours — all free, all running on your machine with data you can inspect, extend and keep. Its voice agent genuinely has no equivalent here: you talk to the globe and it flies, tracks and annotates. For creators, tinkerers and anyone who wants the globe itself to be the experience, nothing hosted matches it.
bAbout: EarthCam runs a network of live webcams anchored by famous places — Times Square in New York is the signature view — organised into destination pages and EarthCam TV channels that package cameras into themed streams. Alongside the free consumer network it sells professional construction-camera systems to businesses, with managed hardware, archiving and time-lapse. Many public cameras are watchable free in the browser and in its mobile apps, with weather information shown alongside some cameras.
bStrengths: EarthCam is the deeper platform for famous places: a large, long-running network of scenic and tourist cameras anchored by Times Square, curated viewing through EarthCam TV, and professional construction-camera services with managed hardware, archiving and time-lapse for commercial clients. For watching a specific famous place — or for a business that needs a camera installed and managed — EarthCam's camera-specific depth and history beat a generalist globe.
betterAnswer: They solve different problems. God's Eye View is a free, open-source 3D globe you run on your own computer — unmatched for immersion, voice control and hackability, with a modest camera layer (~4,000) that is one layer among many. EarthCam is a dedicated webcam portal built for watching: famous landmark cameras and TV-style channels, free to open, with a professional camera business alongside. If you want to *experience* the planet, install God's Eye View; if you want to *watch a famous place* right now, open EarthCam.

No public developer API verified from official sources

faqs.a: No — they are unrelated products. God's Eye View is free open-source software by Bilawal Sidhu and Sameh Khamis that you install and run locally. EarthCam is a hosted live-webcam network. They share a subject — live views of the world — and little else.
faqs.q: Is God's Eye View the same as EarthCam?

faqs.a: Yes. The software is free and open source under the MIT licence. The only costs are optional third-party ones you control: the voice agent uses your own OpenAI API credit (the app warns at $2 and caps at $5 per session), and photoreal 3D tiles can be metered if you use a direct Google key instead of the free Cesium ion route.
faqs.q: Is God's Eye View really free?

faqs.a: EarthCam is the dedicated camera network, built around famous scenic and tourist cameras, though it publishes no audited total. God's Eye View's CCTV Mesh layer states a shared cap of about 4,000 cameras, projected into its 3D scene. For comparison, WorldEye's directory lists 74,229 public cameras.
faqs.q: Which has more live cameras, God's Eye View or EarthCam?

faqs.a: Watching many of EarthCam's public cameras is free in the browser and its apps. EarthCam's paid side is its professional construction-camera business — managed hardware, archiving and time-lapse, quoted per project — rather than a consumer subscription.

faqs.q: Do I need to install anything for EarthCam?

faqs.a: No. EarthCam is a camera directory and player — it has no 3D globe, flight tracking or satellite view. Those are God's Eye View's core layers, and WorldEye also shows cameras on a 3D globe alongside live flights, ships and satellites.

intro: God's Eye View and EarthCam both put live cameras in front of you, but they start from opposite ends. God's Eye View is free, open-source software (by Bilawal Sidhu and Sameh Khamis) that you install on your own computer: a photorealistic 3D globe with live flights, ships, satellites and a camera layer of about 4,000 public cameras projected into the scene. EarthCam is a dedicated webcam portal you simply open in a browser: a large, long-running network of famous scenic and tourist cameras, curated EarthCam TV channels, and professional construction-camera services for businesses.
pricingA: There is no God's Eye View price or subscription — the software is free and open source. The README's own cost table is honest about the edges: most layers cost $0 with no signup; a free-key tier (AISStream, NASA FIRMS, Cesium ion within quota) unlocks more; the voice agent spends your own OpenAI credit with a $2 warning and $5 hard cap per session; and photoreal tiles through a direct Google key are metered by Google.
pricingB: Watching EarthCam's public cameras is free. Its professional construction-camera services, hardware and business offerings are paid and typically quoted per project — there is no consumer subscription comparable to a premium tier.
prosA: Completely free and open source (MIT) — no subscription, ever

seoTitle: God's Eye View vs EarthCam (2026): Local 3D Globe or Famous Webcam Network?

sources.label: God's Eye View — official GitHub repository and README

verdictA: Choose God's Eye View if you want the globe as an experience — photoreal 3D, voice control, cockpit rides, flights, ships and satellites in one scene — you're comfortable installing software, and you want it free and open forever, with cameras as one layer among many.
verdictB: Choose EarthCam if cameras are the whole point — you want famous landmark views like Times Square, curated TV-style channels, or a managed construction-camera service — and you want to just open a browser or an app and watch.
verdictLine: God's Eye View is the spectacle — a photoreal 3D globe you own, where cameras are one layer among many. EarthCam is the specialist — a dedicated webcam network built around famous places. The first is free software you install; the second is a free website built for watching.
worldEye: If installing software is the dealbreaker in God's Eye View, and a camera-only directory is the limit in EarthCam, WorldEye is the middle path: a hosted 3D globe that opens free in any browser with no signup at all — 74,229 public cameras across 109 countries, live flights, ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes and wildfires in the same view. It doesn't render photoreal 3D tiles like God's Eye View or run managed construction cameras like EarthCam, and its Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) buys an OSINT toolkit and intel feeds rather than camera services.
